FROM PASS 15

The whole app

The latest full frame. The CLIO menu is open on the left and the rail is pinned on the right with Context expanded. There's no bottom bar.

FROM PASSES 5, 6 AND 8

Left bar

Conversations replaces the default workspace. ✎ always means a new conversation and + always means a new workspace.

Settled

  • Flat. No box inside a box. Regions are split by full-width lines, and the row you're on is the only highlight.
  • One right edge. Counts, times, spinners, …, ✎ and footer icons all end on the same line.
  • Bare coloured icons for workspaces. Each workspace has its own colour and icon and folds open. Folding is remembered.
  • Collapsing stays. The panel icon shrinks the bar to a 56px icon strip, and it does that by itself when the workbench needs room.
  • Since then: Files and Runs left the bar. The header is one button (pass 15), and workspace settings moved into the Settings dialog (pass 7).
FROM PASS 15

CLIO menu

Shown open in the whole-app frame above. The mark, the name and the line under it are one button that opens one menu.

  • Talking to. The agent you're on, Live or not, then its address, transport, both versions, Up to date with Check again, and Connection settings. Today's Live hover and Updates popover both fold into it.
  • Switch to. Every other saved agent with Online or Offline, and Manage agents beside the heading.
  • Add an agent…. Connect to one that's already running, or start a new one.
  • The line under CLIO reads “CLIO local this computer” and turns amber or red with Reconnecting, Offline or Update ready.
FROM PASS 7

Top bar

The left bar runs to the top and cuts through the bar. That's one row on both web and desktop.

Settled

  • One row, three owners. The left bar's CLIO header, the conversation's breadcrumb, and the right panel's own corner.
  • Desktop adds two things. Back and forward right after the left bar's edge, and the window controls. Any empty part of the row drags the window.
  • Web has no back button of its own. Every view has a real URL, so the browser's back and forward work.
  • The breadcrumb is a menu. The title ⌄ opens the conversation menu, and the workspace name opens the workspace.
  • Since then: the bell is always visible (pass 16). The rail button and the workbench icon are two separate buttons (pass 15), and ✎ replaced + for new conversations (pass 8).
FROM PASS 7

Settings

A dialog, not a page. It dims everything below the top row and never the row itself, so you can still see which workspace and agent you're in. It's grouped by what each setting applies to: the app, this workspace and this agent.

Since then: an App, Notifications page was added with Sound, Desktop alerts and Finished work (pass 16).

FROM PASS 10

New conversation

It works without touching anything except picking a model, and every agent setting is still one click away. There's one line of welcome and no starter prompts.

Since then: mode became an icon (play) with the tooltip “Mode: Execute Ctrl Shift M” (pass 11).

FROM PASS 11

Conversation

No “You” or agent headers. Times show only on hover, and the room that frees up goes to what the agent did.

FROM PASS 12

@ menu

A category rail on the left and results on the right. Delegate items hand one message to someone else, and Reference items attach something.

FROM PASS 14

Conversation rail

It floats over the transcript and stays open, pinned by its button. It's not a popover that closes. It's only as tall as its content.

Settled

  • Plan is the file. It shows plans/soil-comparison.md with its status: Draft, Approved, Done or Abandoned.
  • Todos is the checklist. The agent's todo tool, shown as “2 of 5”, with done items folded away.
  • Two buttons, two jobs. The list icon pins the floating rail, and the panel icon docks the workbench. Both can be open at once.
  • Context expands in place, and “Open full context view” opens today's full page.
FROM PASS 15

Bottom bar

Retired. Everything in it already had a better home.

FROM PASS 16

Notifications

The bell is always there. It has three groups in a fixed order. Toasts are for things you just did, and the bell is for things that happened without you.

Design rules

The rules every pass follows, from your notes along the way.

  • No box inside a box. One surface per menu or dialog, with full-width lines between regions.
  • Bare icons. No tiles behind icons, and no captions under them.
  • No “·” separators. Dots aren't used as decoration either. Read and unread are shown by brightness.
  • One right edge. Everything at the end of a row lines up.
  • ✎ is a new conversation, + is a new workspace.
  • The model is text. The provider logo plus “Provider / model”, with no pill and no chevron. It's a button that opens the full picker.
  • Icons show their state. Anything changed from the default turns teal, and Bypass checks is the only red.
  • Nothing hidden. One button opens one menu. Right-click gives the same menu as ….
  • Hover for detail. Times, actions and the per-reply card only appear on hover.
  • Content-sized floating panels. The rail and menus are only as tall as what's in them.
  • Grounded in the code. Every row maps to something gact-tui already has, or is marked as new.

Open questions

  • “Agent” means two things. It's both the CLIO you're connected to (the left bar) and the setup a conversation runs as (the “with” chip). I'd keep “agent” for the chip only.
  • The workbench (the right panel). It's next, and it gets its own pass. Separately, a fix is in progress for it remembering its width, opening at 40% by default, and collapsing the left bar when space is short.
  • Backend gaps. There's no event yet for a conversation finishing in the background, and notification history isn't stored. Moving a conversation between workspaces and importing into one also need support.
  • Nothing is built yet. All of this is a proposal until you approve it.
